svg.title: The family of an 80-year-old client tells the nurse that the client must be ill because he wakes several times each night and dozes briefly during the day. Which response by the nurse is accurate?
svg.desc: Aging reduces time spent in stage 3 NREM and increases nighttime arousals, so lighter and more fragmented sleep is expected while total sleep need stays near 7 to 8 hours. The option about more deep sleep is the reverse of what happens, and assuming illness without any other findings skips assessment.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Sleep and Aging
Read the situation
The family of an 80-year-old client tells
the nurse that the client must be ill
because he wakes several times each night
and dozes briefly during the day. Which
response by the nurse is accurate?
What fits here
Sleep normally becomes lighter with age,
with more awakenings and less deep sleep
Why it fits
Aging reduces time spent in stage 3 NREM
and increases nighttime arousals, so
lighter and more fragmented sleep is
expected while total sleep need stays near
7 to 8 hours. The option about more deep
sleep is the reverse of what happens, and
assuming illness without any other
findings skips assessment.
